title: Design an accessible colour palette
description: Propose semantic colour pairs for text, surfaces, actions, errors and focus.
accomplishes: Propose semantic colour pairs for text, surfaces, actions, errors and focus. Provide hex values, intended uses and a contrast verification procedure. Never use colour alone to communicate state or claim a measured ratio without calculating it.
prompt:
Act as a senior product designer.

Task: Design an accessible colour palette.

Input context:
- BRAND: [BRAND]
- SURFACES: [SURFACES]
- TEXT ROLES: [TEXT ROLES]

Propose semantic colour pairs for text, surfaces, actions, errors and focus. Provide hex values, intended uses and a contrast verification procedure. Never use colour alone to communicate state or claim a measured ratio without calculating it.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Palette proposal
Use navy text on white for reading, blue for primary actions and a pale neutral surface for grouping. Error messages combine an icon, label and explanation rather than red alone. Check every foreground/background combination, including hover and focus. Keep the proposal provisional until actual contrast values and visual states have been verified.
